function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a national delivery service.

---

## 1️⃣ Local & Specialty Bakeries  
These are often the best choice for fresh, custom‑made cakes and unique flavors.

| Option | What Makes Them Stand Out | How to Order |
|--------|--------------------------|--------------|
| **Your neighborhood bakery** | Fresh ingredients, personalized service, often offers same‑day pickup or delivery. | Call or visit their website; many now accept online orders via their own site or platforms like Square Online. |
| **Artisan cake shops** (e.g., “The Cake Studio,” “Sweet & Savory”) | Custom designs, themed cakes, vegan/gluten‑free options. | Browse their portfolio online, then email or call to discuss your vision. |
| **Specialty dessert cafés** (e.g., “ChocoLuxe,” “Patisserie Parisienne”) | Signature pastries, high‑end chocolate or French patisserie styles. | Book through their website or a phone reservation; they’ll confirm availability and delivery details. |

> **Tip:** Check Google Maps or Yelp for recent reviews, photos, and delivery radius. Many local shops also post on Instagram or Facebook—just search the shop’s name plus “delivery” or “online order.”

---

## 2️⃣ National Chains & Big Brands  
Great for standardized quality, nationwide coverage, and sometimes free delivery.

| Brand | Strengths | Ordering Method |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| **T.G.I. Friday’s** | Classic American cakes, often free delivery within a certain radius. | Order online at tgi-friday.com or via the TGI Friday’s app. |
| **Dunkin’ Donuts** | Quick delivery, especially if you’re already a member of their loyalty program. | Use the Dunkin’ app or website; select “Cake” from the menu. |
| **Panera Bread** | Fresh, made‑to‑order cakes, good for dietary restrictions. | Order through Panera’s website or app; choose “Custom Cakes.” |
| **Cinnabon** | Known for cinnamon rolls, but they also offer small cakes and cupcakes. | Order online or call your nearest store. |

> **Note:** Delivery fees and minimum orders vary by location. Some chains partner with delivery apps (DoorDash, Uber Eats) for broader coverage.

---

## 3️⃣ Online Delivery Platforms  
If you want a wide selection without leaving your home.

| Platform | Highlights | How to Find Cakes |
|----------|------------|-------------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated selection from top U.S. bakeries, nationwide shipping. | Search “cake” + your ZIP code; filter by flavor, size, dietary needs. |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, artisanal cakes from independent bakers worldwide. | Search “custom cake” + your location; contact sellers directly for delivery arrangements. |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Fresh baked goods delivered same day in select cities. | Search “cake” in Amazon Fresh; choose “Fresh” under “Delivery Options.” |
| **Instacart** | Partner with local grocery stores that carry pre‑made cakes. | Add a cake to your cart; Instacart will pick it up and deliver. |

> **Pro tip:** For special occasions, Etsy sellers often allow you to upload a photo of your design idea—great for truly custom cakes!

---

## 4️⃣ Specialty & Dietary‑Focused Options  
If you have specific dietary requirements or want a niche flavor.

| Category | Example Shops | Why Choose Them |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| **Vegan & Gluten‑Free** | “Baker’s Delight Vegan Bakery,” “Gluten‑Free Goodness.” | Certified allergen‑free, often use organic ingredients. |
| **Low‑Sugar / Keto** | “Keto Kitchen,” “Sugarless Sweet.” | Low‑carb, sugar‑free frosting options. |
| **Ethnic & Fusion** | “Sweets of India,” “Mexican Munchies.” | Authentic regional flavors (gulab jamun, tres leches). |

> **How to Order:** Most of these shops have dedicated ordering pages; otherwise, email or call to discuss your dietary needs.

---

## 5️⃣ Tips for a Smooth Cake Order

1. **Plan Ahead** – Especially for custom designs, order at least 1–2 weeks in advance.  
2. **Confirm Delivery Details** – Ask about delivery windows, packaging, and whether the cake arrives fully assembled or requires assembly.  
3. **Check Reviews** – Look for recent photos and comments about freshness, taste, and customer service.  
4. **Ask About Allergens** – If you’re ordering for a group, confirm that the bakery can accommodate allergies or dietary restrictions.  
5. **Keep the Contact Info** – Save the bakery’s phone number or email in case you need to tweak the order last minute.

---

### Quick Starter List (U.S. Nationwide)

| City | Recommended Bakery | Website |
|------|--------------------|---------|
| New York | Levain Bakery | levainbakery.com |
| Los Angeles | Baked by Melissa | bakedbymelissa.com |
| Chicago | Magnolia Bakery | magnolia-bakery.com |
| Houston | The Cake Shop | thecakeshop.com |
| Seattle | Sweet Treats Bakery | sweettreats.com |

*(If you let me know your city or ZIP code, I can narrow down the best local options for you.)*

Happy cake hunting! 🎂
